A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSB research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy and throughput experiments across four models and five benchmarks, alongside cache and scheduling ablations, including the suffix-window appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results, adds evaluated baselines, and reports original measurements of late and premature decoding in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same sliding-boundary updates, constant and greedy variants, prefix-window refresh, and periodic global cache refresh. The experimental suffix window remains excluded from the final method in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, and BBH. The new motivation analysis reuses GSM8K and HumanEval with existing models and task conditions; it does not introduce a distinct dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 1–2 add AdaBlock-dLLM without caching and with Dual Cache, plus dKV-Cache-Decode with naive blocks, across all four models and five benchmarks. These methods were discussed but not evaluated in v2, substantially broadening comparisons for both scheduling and caching.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces a diagnostic protocol using 50 samples from each of GSM8K and HumanEval and counting decoding events against a 0.9 confidence threshold at every step. The existing main experiments retain their few-shot settings, models, generation length, block settings, and accuracy/TPS metrics.

E4.justification: New Appendix A and Figure 8 directly measure whether fixed blocks delay confident outside positions or commit uncertain inside positions. Existing ablations remain, with revised Dream results in the generation-length and maximum-block-length analyses. The suffix-window study is retained as Appendix B and Figure 9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new appendix adds event-frequency point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline results and diagnostic frequencies and revises numerous existing accuracies. Cached LLaDA-8B-Instruct DSB (greedy) MBPP accuracy changes from 27.40 to 42.80. On Dream-Base HumanEval, cached DSB (const.) changes from 42.07 to 52.44, now tying Dual Cache, whose accuracy changes from 36.59 to 52.44. Dream accuracy plots in Figures 5–6 also change. The PDFs do not explain these revisions or establish improvements from a changed method.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces threshold-based definitions of late and premature steps and their step-fraction metrics, including Late Ratio = Late Step / Total Step. These are limited new diagnostic definitions; existing decoding mathematics and assumptions remain unchanged, and no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free DSB improves scheduling, and its tailored cache improves the quality–speed trade-off. Additional comparisons and motivation evidence support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 narrows its overall characterization from improvements across all settings to most settings. Section 5.3 explicitly acknowledges accuracy exceptions at initial block length 64 and LLaDA generation length 1024. New Section 6 discusses maximum-block-length dependence and practical variant choices, while formalizing the Dream-without-cache inconsistency already noted in v2.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new appendix analysis’s sample counts, confidence computation over masked positions, event criteria, and normalization. The main hardware, lm-eval implementation, DSB hyperparameters, and code-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds WavefrontDiffusion and DAWN, removes the citation to Kong et al.’s local determinism propagation work, and expands discussion of already-cited Fast-dLLM v2, AdaBlock, and WeDLM. These clarify distinctions among block scheduling approaches while retaining DSB’s overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related work and experimental discussion. v3 adds a Limitations section and motivation appendix, renames the retained appendices, and replaces the preprint notice with proceedings text. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main table is split into LLaDA and Dream tables with additional comparator rows and red highlighting. The cache-ablation table and existing figures are relocated, and a diagnostic bar chart is added. Figure 6 changes its Dream accuracy axis and drops the cache designation; Figure 5’s caption explicitly names DSB Cache.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support by evaluating relevant scheduling and caching alternatives and adding a documented motivation check. Its explicit accuracy exceptions also make the discussion better match the figures. These provide a clear but bounded quality gain: substantial accuracy revisions remain unexplained, and the new diagnostic lacks uncertainty reporting.
